newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends lower after two-way business.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends lower after two-way business.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended Thursday a shade below New York's Wednesday close after a day of lacklustre trade, bullion dealers said.
"In the pre-opening, we saw some New York selling which pushed the market down to US$382.50/85 per ounce," said one trader at an international bank's local office.
But interested buyers sprang into action after Asian trade opened, pushing the market up to around $383 per ounce, gold traders said.
Trade was bound tightly within a range, with strong support at about $381.50 and resistance at $384.50, dealers said.
The market saw small two-way business but local professionals and overseas players remained mostly on the sidelines, they said.
"We believe the (U.S.) funds have not fully covered their short positions," said one gold trader, noting his view of the market trended towards bullishness.
Some bullion dealers reported light physical demand at the lower end of the range.
Bullion ended at $383.00/50 an ounce on Thursday against New York's $383.05/45 close on Wednesday.
Local gold ended HK$4 higher at HK$3,528 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped from -5.00 to -6.00.
